title: Aligned but Not Partner-Specific: Distinguishing How Multimodal LLM Agents Succeed in Reference Games Without Human-Like Conventions
one_sentence: 用打断 partner history 的 constrained pseudo-dyad baseline 证明高 lexical overlap 和成功可在没有 partner-specific convention 时出现。
problem: MLLM reference-game alignment 来自具体 dyad 的 shared history，还是共享任务 vocabulary、pretrained priors 与 verbosity？
method: 比较 45 个 GPT-5 MLLM dyads/905 rounds 与 42 个 human dyads/3,288 rounds，并构造匹配 referent、round、turn count 与 success 的 pseudo-dyads。
findings: Humans 随互动压缩表达，real dyads 相对 pseudo-dyads 显示 interaction-dependent reuse。
Agents 保持冗长；real/pseudo overlap 近 ceiling 且无可靠差异，说明 coordination 可不依赖具体 partner history。
real_contribution: 提供可反事实检验 partner-specific origin 的 history-severing diagnostic，而非仅以 success、compression 或 overlap 命名 convention。
biggest_weakness: preprint；使用单一 GPT-5 setup 与 agent-agent dyads，没有 human–AI mixed condition。
claim_boundary: 支持‘alignment/coordination 不足以证明 convention’，但不能推出所有模型或所有 training regimes 都缺乏 partner-specific grounding。
why_researcher_should_care: 几乎直接提供 GAP-04/GAP-07 所需的核心 diagnostic，并迫使 AMSC novelty 使用反事实 history test。
evidence_notes: arXiv v1 from June 2026; outside the strict seven-day window and labeled first-run recovery.
Preprint status is preserved; full text and reported mixed-effects results were audited.
